children: Shares of Chinese automaker Li Auto rose sharply after it reported improved third-quarter margins and said it expects to return to profitability in the fourth quarter.
The shares gained 12% to 47.46 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to $6.05, early Thursday, putting them on track for their largest one-day percentage gain since February 2025.
Li Auto reported a third-quarter gross margin of 16.7% and a vehicle gross margin of 15.3%, helped by a more profitable mix of models sold.
"With improving financials in the third quarter and considering the successful launch of the new i6, we believe Li Auto is on track to show a recovery trend ahead," Nomura analysts wrote in a note.

Bernstein analysts said cost savings from Li Auto's Bianshan battery also helped lift margins. They said management expects the company to return to profitability in the fourth quarter, though Bernstein sees a challenging outlook for 2027.
Demand is slowing in China's auto market, and Li Auto's shift from plug-in hybrids to fully electric vehicles could weigh on both sales volumes and gross margins, Bernstein said.
Li Auto is expanding overseas to boost sales. It has entered markets in Central Asia and the Middle East and is rolling out vehicles in Southeast Asia and Europe.
